'''Frank Gibbs Tetteh O'Baka Torto''', [[Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences|FGA]], [[Order of the Volta|MV]] (10 October 1921 – May  1984) was a [[Ghanaian]] [[chemist]] and a [[professor]] at the [[University of Ghana]]. He was a founding member, vice president and later president of the [[Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. He was the first Ghanaian lecturer of the [[University of Ghana]].

==Early life and education==
Frank Gibbs Torto was born on 10 October 1921 in [[Accra]].<ref name="TETTEH" />

He was educated in many elementary schools in the [[Gold Coast (British colony)|Gold Coast]]. In 1931, he enrolled at the [[Accra Academy]] as one of the school's foundation students.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Mensah |first1=J. N. A. |date=2013 |title=Traditions and customs of Gadangmes of Ghana : descendants of authentic Biblical Hebrew Israelites |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8tYeAgAAQBAJ&q=torto+accra+academy&pg=PA277 |page=277|publisher=Strategic Book |isbn=9781628571042 }}</ref> He completed in 1936 and joined the intermediate department of [[Achimota School|Achimota College]] a year later to pursue an intermediate [[bachelor's degree]] which he received in 1941. In 1942, he proceeded to the [[United Kingdom]] for his tertiary education. He was accepted into the [[Queen Mary University of London]] a constituent college of the [[University of London]] studying there from the bachelors level; graduating with first class honours<ref>{{cite book |title=Proceedings of the Ghana Academy of Sciences. |publisher=Secretariat of the Ghana Academy of Sciences, 1964-1968 |page=17 |date=1963}}</ref> to doctorate level, he was awarded his doctorate (Ph.D.) degree in chemistry in 1947.<ref name="OBAKA">{{cite book |last1=Uwechue |first1=Ralph |title=Africa Who's who |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9EAOAQAAMAAJ&q=frank+gibbs+tetteh+obaka+torto |publisher=Africa Journal Limited |page=1735 |date=1991|isbn=9780903274173 }}</ref><ref name= "TETTEH">{{cite book |title=International book of honor |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=d8_F3KRx3iIC&q=frank+gibbs+torto |publisher=American Biographical Institute |page=373 |date=1987|isbn = 9780934544320}}</ref><ref name= "FRANK">{{cite book |title=Ghana Year Book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=njAuAQAAIAAJ&q=frank+gibbs+torto |publisher=Graphic Corporation |page=286 |date=1978}}</ref><ref name="F G T O TORTO">{{cite book |title=Who's who in the world |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3foKAQAAMAAJ&q=Torto |publisher=Wilmette, Ill. : Marquis Who's Who, Macmillan Directory Division |page=696 |date=1978|isbn = 9780837911038}}</ref>

==Career==
He returned to Ghana in 1947 after his studies abroad and joined the faculty of Achimota College's intermediate department as a lecturer. A year later when the University College of the Gold Coast was founded he together with [[Walter Warwick Sawyer]], D. K. Baldwin and Mary C. Charnley all from the Intermediate department were appointed as the first group of staff to form the nucleus of the university's teaching faculty<ref>{{cite book |last1=Agbodeka |first1=Francis |date=1998 |title=A history of University of Ghana: half a century of higher education (1948-1998) |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=l9wsAQAAIAAJ&q=torto+chemistry+first |page=45|publisher=Woeli Pub. Services |isbn=9789964978563 }}</ref> thereby making him the first Ghanaian lecturer of the university.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Agbodeka |first1=Francis |date=1998 |title=A history of University of Ghana: half a century of higher education (1948-1998) |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=l9wsAQAAIAAJ&q=+member+consider+whole |page=217|publisher=Woeli Pub. Services |isbn=9789964978563 }}</ref> He was a lecturer of chemistry at the university in 1948 and a [[senior lecturer]] in 1957. He became a Ghana [[UNESCO]] National Commission member in 1958 and in 1959 became a founding member of the [[Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences]].  
 
A year later, he was appointed a scientific consultant for the [[United Nations]]. In 1962, he rose to professorship status and the head of the chemistry department.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Addy |first1=M. A. |authorlink=Marian Ewurama Addy |date=2011 |title=Rewards : an autobiography |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9gpkHOFb5DwC&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe&pg=PA320 |page=48|publisher=African Books Collective |isbn=9789988037826 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Feeding Africa: Proceedings of the Second Symposium of Pan African Pugwash Group, 28th May - 3rd June 1978, Cape Coast University, Ghana |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lEwCAAAAMAAJ&q=f+g+torto |publisher=Pan African Pugwash Group |page=18 |date=1978}}</ref> That same year, he was named with [[Stephen Oluwole Awokoya]] by the then [[Secretary-General of the United Nations]]; [[U Thant]] among eight scientific secretaries for a United Nations conference on the application of science and technology for the benefit of less developed areas, a conference that was held in [[Geneva]], [[Switzerland]].<ref>{{cite book |title=West Africa, Issues 2328-2352 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EBkOAQAAMAAJ&q=f+g+torto |publisher=Afrimedia International |page=194 |date=1962}}</ref> In 1965, he was appointed president of the Ghana Science Association and a year later, president of the Association of Science Teachers.<ref>{{cite book |title=Ghana Year Book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KDAuAQAAIAAJ&q=f+g+torto |publisher=Graphic Corporation |page=275 |date=1967}}</ref>

In October 1968, he was a visiting fellow at [[Churchill College]], [[University of Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Cambridge University Reporter, Volume 98, Issue 3 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=S9cDI8t2d4sC&q=f+g+torto |publisher=University of Cambridge |page=2562 |date=1968}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Register |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=n32NIwBTM6IC&q=frank+gibbs+torto |publisher=Cambridge Auxiliary Fire Department |page=640 |date=1970}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=The Cambridge University List of Members for the Year |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=05AcAQAAMAAJ&q=Torto |publisher=Cambridge Auxiliary Fire Department |page=1366 |date=1991| isbn=978-0-521-43468-3 }}</ref> He was then appointed dean of the faculty of Science at the University of Ghana in 1969 taking over from [[Alan Nunn May]], he served in this capacity until 1971.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Daniel |first1=Ebow |date=1999 |title=Mr. Registrar : the making of an amanuensis |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JOwsAQAAIAAJ&q=f+g+torto |page=120|publisher=Woeli Pub. Services |isbn=9789964978594 }}</ref> In 1972, he became a member of the continuing committee of the [[Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Proceedings of the Twenty-Fifth Pugwash Conference on Science and World Affairs: Development, Resources and World Security, Madras, India, 13-19 January, 1976 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-w0KAQAAIAAJ&q=frank+torto |publisher=Pugwash Conference on Science and World Affairs |page=62 |date=1976}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Rotblat |first1=Joseph |authorlink=Joseph Rotblat |date=1972 |title=Crisis, Change, and Revolution in Ghanaian Education |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BbLaAAAAMAAJ&q=frank+torto |page=89|isbn=9780262180542 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Pugwash Newsletter, Volume 24-25 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=l58kAQAAIAAJ&q=f+g+torto |publisher=Council of the Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs |page=ii |date=1974}}</ref> In 1973, he was made dean of the faculty of science for a second occasion.<ref>{{cite book |author=Unesco. Regional Office of Science and Technology for Africa. |date=1975 |title=Final Report |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UcaIrqgE-LUC&q=f+g+torto}}</ref> This time he served in that capacity for a year. In 1978, he served on the [[United Nations]] advisory committee on Science, Technology and Global Problems.<ref>{{cite book |title=Oficial Records, Volume 1 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5_5o8vdvAwYC&q=f+g+torto |publisher=United Nations. Economic and Social Council |page=243 |date=1978}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Stuart |first1=Sam |date=2016 |title=Science, Technology and Global Problems: The United Nations Advisory |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Zel3DAAAQBAJ&q=f+g+torto+london&pg=PA60 |page=60|publisher=Elsevier |isbn=9781483189451 }}</ref>

In 1979, he was appointed chairman  of the board of the Ghana National Manganese Corporation. That same year, he was appointed vice president of the [[Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. He served in this capacity until 1981 when he was appointed president of the academic body.
   
In his lifetime, Torto served on various other committees and organizations some of which include; the [[Council for Scientific and Industrial Research – Ghana]] and the Council of the [[Centre for Scientific Research into Plant Medicine]]. He was also an editorial board member for the West African Journal of Biological and Applied Chemistry.<ref>{{cite book |title=West African Journal of Biological and Applied Chemistry, Volumes 6-11 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xsRFAAAAYAAJ&q=f+g+torto |publisher=J. M. P. Services |page=71 |date=1962}}</ref><ref name="OBAKA"/><ref name="TETTEH"/><ref name="FRANK"/><ref name="F G T O TORTO"/>

==Honours and legacies==
He was a recipient of the member of the [[Order of the Volta]] award.<ref name= "TETTEH"/>

The University of Ghana award for best graduating student in chemistry is named after him.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ug.edu.gh/academic-prize-awards-20132014 |title=Academic Prize Awards – 2013/2014 |publisher=UNIVERSITY OF GHANA |access-date=12 April 2019 |archive-date=12 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412035841/https://www.ug.edu.gh/academic-prize-awards-20132014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The University of Ghana Chemistry building was also named in his honour.<ref>{{cite book |title=Annual Report |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=L6clAQAAIAAJ&q=frank+torto |publisher=State Publishing Company |page=xxxviii |date=2007}}</ref>

==Works==
Frank authored many articles that were published in scientific and general publications. His works have been featured in journals such as; the [[Journal of the Chemical Society]], [[Nature (journal)]], West African Journal of Biological Science and the Ghana Journal of Science.<ref>{{cite book |title=Ghana Journal of Science: A Joint Publication of the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research and the Ghana Science Association, Volumes 7-12 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7jG5AAAAIAAJ&q=f+g+torto |publisher=Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (Ghana) |page=3 |date=1967}}</ref> Some of his works include;

*(contrib.) ''Some Problems in the Study of Plant Gum Polyssacharides'', 1960;<ref>{{cite book |title=West African Journal of Biological Chemistry, Volumes 4-5 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UYIIAQAAIAAJ&q=f+g+torto |publisher=University College |page=6 |date=1960}}</ref>
*(contrib.) ''An Aldobiouronic Acid Isolated from Fagara xanthoxyloides Gum'', 1961;<ref>{{cite book |title=Journal of the Chemical Society |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yKpm4Ld4oQoC&q=f+g+torto |publisher=Chemical Society |page=3166 |date=1961}}</ref>
*(contrib.) ''The training of scientists in Ghana" in scientific world'', 1964;<ref>{{cite book |title=scientific world vol VIII, No. 4 |pages=3–8 |date=1964}}</ref>
*(contrib.) ''Arms and African Development'' Ed. F S Arkhurst: Praeger, 1972;<ref name="OBAKA"/>
*(contrib.) ''Views of Science Technology and Development'' Ed. V. Rabinowitch: Pergamon, 1975;<ref name="OBAKA"/>
* ''Structure of the Alkaloid Wisanine (2-Methoxypiperine)'', 1981;<ref name= "TETTEH"/>
* ''University Chemistry in Developing Countries'', 1981;<ref name= "TETTEH"/>

==Personal life==
Frank married Iris Aku Torto (''née'' Akwei) in 1949. Together they had three children; Oboshie Adjua Torto, Obodai Torto and Ofori Torto. He enjoyed listening to music in his spare time, and played classical piano.<ref name="OBAKA"/><ref name= "TETTEH"/><ref name= "FRANK"/> He died in May 1984.<ref>{{cite book |title=Proceedings of the Pugwash Conference on Science and World Affairs., Volume 35 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-qEkAQAAIAAJ&q=frank+torto |publisher=Pugwash Conference on Science and World Affairs |page=45 |date=1985}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Pugwash Newsletter, Volume 22 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZD9DAQAAIAAJ&q=frank+torto |publisher=Council of the Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs |page=111 |date=1985}}</ref>
